problem_text:
A city planner needs to distribute a fixed budget across 19 different infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.  
The profile for each project is as follows:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.048, impact factor 0.269, allocation limits [0.040, 0.740]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.111, impact factor 0.064, allocation limits [0.059, 0.828]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.185, impact factor 0.018, allocation limits [0.053, 0.461]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.059, impact factor 0.202, allocation limits [0.049, 0.423]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.085, impact factor 0.141, allocation limits [0.043, 0.771]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.196, impact factor 0.087, allocation limits [0.068, 0.509]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.176, impact factor 0.279, allocation limits [0.065, 0.473]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.112, impact factor 0.034, allocation limits [0.096, 0.658]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.160, impact factor 0.135, allocation limits [0.022, 0.740]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.054, impact factor 0.054, allocation limits [0.005, 0.357]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.070, impact factor 0.156, allocation limits [0.004, 0.602]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.050, impact factor 0.157, allocation limits [0.027, 0.720]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.075, impact factor 0.025, allocation limits [0.007, 0.586]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.177, impact factor 0.089, allocation limits [0.010, 0.483]  
* Project O: benefit score 0.137, impact factor 0.038, allocation limits [0.023, 0.844]  
* Project P: benefit score 0.047, impact factor 0.198, allocation limits [0.062, 0.443]  
* Project Q: benefit score 0.178, impact factor 0.222, allocation limits [0.072, 0.489]  
* Project R: benefit score 0.154, impact factor 0.133, allocation limits [0.039, 0.342]  
* Project S: benefit score 0.063, impact factor 0.095, allocation limits [0.010, 0.412]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified allocation limits, and the sum of all budget shares must equal the total available budget of 1.  
To prioritize visible public works, the planner requires that the group of high-visibility projects, represented by the subset V = {B, E, F, M, N, P, Q, S}, must together receive at least 0.522 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the total community disruption, measured by a composite impact index, must not exceed 0.160, and the total benefit score of the portfolio must be at least 0.086.  
Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
